Infer a pinnable schema from a data frame

Source: R/schema_infer.R
infsch.Rd

Derives the schema valsch() consumes from data you already trust, so a capsule can be pinned without writing one by hand. Infer it once from the extract the analysis was run on, read it, edit it, commit it, and validate every later download against it.

Usage

infsch(data, slack = 0.1, maxlvl = 50L)

Arguments

data

A data frame to learn from.

slack

Headroom, one non-negative number (default 0.1). It is a fraction of the row count and of each numeric range, and an absolute amount added to each missingness rate (0.1 allows ten more percentage points of NA). 0 pins exactly to what was observed, which will reject almost any re-release.

maxlvl

Maximum distinct values for a categorical column to have its value set recorded, one positive whole number (default 50). Above this the column is treated as free text and no value set is pinned.

Value

A list of class bricklayer_schema with these elements:

  • expected_columns (character);

  • expected_types (named character);

  • structural_invariants (list of min_data_rows and max_data_rows, integers);

  • expected_value_sets (named list of character vectors);

  • numeric_ranges (named list of c(min =, max =));

  • max_missing_fraction (named numeric).

Wrap it as list(schema = <this>) to hand to valsch().

Details

What it records: the column names and their types, row-count bounds with slack either side, the observed value set for every low-cardinality categorical column, the observed range of every numeric column widened by slack, and the observed missingness rate per column with headroom.

The rules, with \(n\) rows:

  • types: the first class of each column ("integer", "numeric", "character", "factor", "Date", ...);

  • rows: min_data_rows \(= \lfloor n(1 - slack) \rfloor\) (at least 0) and max_data_rows \(= \lceil n(1 + slack) \rceil\);

  • numeric ranges: \([lo - pad, hi + pad]\) with \(pad = slack \times (hi - lo)\), or \(slack \times \max(|lo|, 1)\) for a constant column; a column with no non-missing value gets no range;

  • value sets: for character, factor and logical columns with at most maxlvl distinct non-missing values, those values as sorted text;

  • missingness: the observed share of NA plus slack (added, not multiplied), capped at 1.

Other column types (dates, lists) get a type and a missingness ceiling only.

This is a starting point, not an oracle

An inferred schema describes ONE extract. It cannot know that a category which happens not to occur is nonetheless legal, or that a range is a physical bound rather than an accident of this sample. Read what it produces and edit it before committing – the value is in not starting from a blank file, not in trusting the output blindly.

Errors: data not a data frame or without columns; slack not one non-negative number; maxlvl not one positive whole number.

See also

valsch(), cpsdrft() for the distributional check the schema cannot make.

Examples

set.seed(1)
df <- data.frame(
  id = 1:100,
  score = stats::runif(100, 0, 10),
  grade = sample(c("a", "b", "c"), 100, TRUE),
  note = paste0("free text ", 1:100),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

sch <- infsch(df)
sch
#> ── Inferred schema ───────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   columns         4
#>   rows            90 to 111
#>   value sets      1
#>   numeric ranges  2
#> 
#>   id                   integer    max NA  10.0%  [ -8.9, 109.9]
#>   score                numeric    max NA  10.0%  [-0.8446,  10.9]
#>   grade                character  max NA  10.0%  a, b, c
#>   note                 character  max NA  10.0%  – free
#> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# The categorical column has its levels pinned; the free-text one does
# not, because it exceeds max_levels.
sch$expected_value_sets
#> $grade
#> [1] "a" "b" "c"
#> 

# It validates the data it was learned from.
length(valsch(df, list(schema = sch)))
#> [1] 0

# And catches a column that has gone missing, or a new category.
length(valsch(df[, -3], list(schema = sch))) > 0
#> [1] TRUE
bad <- df; bad$grade[1] <- "z"
length(valsch(bad, list(schema = sch))) > 0
#> [1] TRUE

# no slack pins the exact observed range
infsch(df, slack = 0)$numeric_ranges$score
#>       min       max 
#> 0.1339033 9.9190609 

# a negative slack is refused
try(infsch(df, slack = -0.1))
#> Error : `slack` must be a single non-negative number
